texts: good. it becomes a fireable rule — every Keeper gets their own tending and their own station — and "alone" is carried as a manner tag rather than dropped.
good. the when-clause becomes a fireable rule: each training occasion yields one joint tending with the Keeper and the apprentice both as doers, tied to that training.

mixed: the pairing itself is right — a two-Keeper group tending the named lantern together — but "during high-wraith weeks" collapses into a single time tag on one tending, so the recurring arrangement (that this holds in every such week) is not recoverable. Rewrite it as a when-clause, the shape that worked in the apprentice sentence above: "When a week is a high-wraith week, two Keepers tend the Stilllight Lantern together."

mixed: faithful as written, and the beginning is correctly an event with a sundown time, but "a night shift" mints one anonymous shift, so the parse says nothing about night shifts in general and produces no rule. If this is the standing schedule, use a bare plural: "Night shifts begin at sundown."

mixed: the check, the keeper, the lantern and the midnight slot are all covered, but "A Keeper" mints one anonymous keeper, so this never reaches a named Keeper elsewhere in the lore and no rule is produced. If every Keeper does this at their own station, write "Each Keeper checks the lantern at midnight." — the phrasing that gave a proper rule in the first sentence; if only whichever Keeper is on duty does it, leave the sentence as it stands.

mixed: same shape and same caveat as the midnight sentence — everything is covered and "the third watch" is kept as a named time, but the indefinite "A Keeper" gives one anonymous keeper rather than a rule. Use "Each Keeper checks the lantern at the third watch." if it is meant to hold for all Keepers.

bad: the ending is stored only as an interval endpoint hung on the shift, with no ending event at all, so the end cannot be queried, ordered or timed the way the sundown sentence's beginning can — the start and end of one shift land in incompatible shapes. Rewrite with the wording that interval form is actually built for: "The shift runs until dawn." (The sentence as written is also fine English — the intended reading is an ending event with the shift as its subject and dawn as its time — but the current parse does not produce it.)
